transcript:
Header: 2026-05-06 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Atlas Head of ML), Dan Walker (Atlas SRE), Sofia Lopez (Atlas CTO)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a 45 minute runthrough of the console tracing, error analysis and request logs, and then leave time for questions. Maya's gonna do most of the demo.
[00:12] Priya: Thanks Alex, excited — we've been seeing occasional 500 spikes on inference calls, and want a better debugging flow.
[00:20] Maya: Great, I'll start with the tracing tab. So this is the per-request trace view, you can see timeline of kernels, batching, kv-cache hits, and routing decisions. Note that some of our auto labels come from heuristics so names might be slightly off — e.g., it says KVCache instead of KV cache sometimes in the UI.
[00:41] Dan: Quick q — can we correlate traces with our internal request ids? We pass x-request-id in header.
[00:50] Maya: Yep, there's a searchable request header field; I'll filter by x-request-id now. (typing) here's a trace that matches the id you sent earlier. You'll see the request landed on a shared pool, routed to model-rw-7, then there was a retry to model-rw-6 due to a node transient.
[01:12] Sofia: How often does that retry happen? It looks like a fallback which could increase latency.
[01:18] Maya: Correct. We have routing policies — in this case warm fallback was triggered because the primary capacity returned a 503. The trace shows the first attempt had 504 from the GPU runtime. You can expand the step to see logs and the exact kernel error message (we sometimes transcribe the runtime message but it's not a perfect verbatim).
[01:40] Priya: Are these RBAC-protected? We need only ops and security to see raw logs.
[01:45] Alex: Yes, we support RBAC and SSO/SAML integration; the console respects customer roles. We'll share the security guide.
[01:52] Maya: Back to error analysis — on the right there's an error histogram and a link to correlated request logs. If you click the 500 spike timeframe it auto-filters logs and shows traces ordered by latency and error class.
[02:10] Dan: That's helpful. Can we export a set of traces and attach to our ticketing system?
[02:15] Maya: Yes export as json or csv; you can also copy a permalink to a trace which respects your team's access controls.
[02:24] Priya: We saw sample highlights in onboarding where Redwood suggested batching and quantization changes — will the console recommend those automatically?
[02:33] Maya: There's the Optimize suggestions tab — it surfaces batching, cache TTL, and quantization profiles per route. For production we usually recommend running a short eval and Redwood Optimize will produce suggestions with estimated latency/cost impact. That's a separate walkthrough but we can link it.
[02:50] Sofia: On data protection — do request logs contain PII? We plan to scrub request text before shipping.
[02:57] Alex: Customers control retention and can enable in-flight scrubbing; Redwood also supports KMS for logs at rest and audit logs for access. We'll send the compliance doc.
[03:10] Maya: Now I'll show a debugging scenario: spike at 10:12 UTC, many requests returned 500. (navigates) Here on the request logs you can see payload size, model variant, quantization, and per-token timing. Notice several requests had sudden tokenization failures — those are labeled 'tokenize-ex' in the trace but sometimes the transcription calls it 'token-eys' by mistake.
[03:38] Dan: Could be malformed input from upstream, we have a gateway that rewrites headers.
[03:42] Priya: We also saw CPU-bound GC but not sure where that occurred.
[03:46] Maya: You can correlate to infra metrics in the same timeline — GPU memory, CPU, host OOMs. The trace shows a host OOM at attempt 1, then a fallback to a different host.
[04:03] Alex: For dedicated capacity, those fallback policies can be changed so requests don't leave the dedicated pool — that's often a priority for customers with strict latency needs.
[04:12] Sofia: Pricing question — do we pay different for fallbacks to hosted?
[04:16] Alex: Yes if you use Dedicated + sudden spillover to hosted, billing splits by capacity type; we can show sample cost scenarios. I'll include pricing examples.
[04:28] Maya: Also note the request-logs view can be filtered by model version pinned to a route; that helps during rollouts/canary. You can compare error rates across versions side-by-side.
[04:45] Priya: Can we set automated alerts when error-rate crosses threshold for a route?
[04:49] Maya: Absolutely. There's alerting integrated with Slack/PagerDuty. Alerts can include a trace sample and links to a pinned debugging playbook.
[04:59] Dan: Is there a way to replay requests against a different model for A/B testing?
[05:03] Maya: You can export traces and replay in a sandboxed replay tool we provide or run a controlled canary through the route config. The replay will anonymize PII if you enable that flag.
[05:15] Priya: For our compliance team we need audit logs of who looked at traces.
[05:19] Alex: We keep audit logs and retention controls; they export to your SIEM via S3/secure stream.
[05:25] Maya: I'm going to show the trace detail — this one failed with kernel OOM; expanded step shows kernel name, stack, approximate memory usage, and a suggestion item 'reduce batch size or switch quant profile'.
[05:41] Priya: What's the usual TTR (time to resolution) when we hand these artifacts to Redwood support?
[05:46] Alex: For enterprise SLAs we have a 4-hour initial response on P1s; we'll confirm in the contract.
[05:52] Sofia: Can we get a short POC to run your tracing on our traffic for a week?
[05:57] Alex: Yes common path is a week-long pilot using a mirrored traffic sample — costs vary but we'll propose options (hosted pilot vs dedicated trial).
[06:05] Maya: I'll also point out the debug timeline has a link to request payload (if permitted), and an obfuscated version for security reviewers.
[06:14] Dan: Any gotchas about sampling? If we sample 1% of traces, we might miss rare errors.
[06:20] Maya: Right — sampling strategy matters. We support dynamic sampling where you can increase sampling for high-error routes or escalate sampling on anomaly detection.
[06:31] Priya: Do you do anomaly detection on traces itself or only on aggregated metrics?
[06:36] Maya: Both. We run anomaly detection on error patterns and latency distributions and can surface correlated trace clusters.
[06:44] Alex: Quick demo wrap: we'll send the recording, pricing, security docs, and next-steps. Any last questions?
[06:51] Priya: Could we get a short checklist for onboarding traces to be compliant?
[06:56] Alex: Yes we'll share onboarding checklist and playbook.
[07:00] Sofia: Thanks, looks promising.

Recap (automated): 1) Demo of tracing + error analysis + request logs. 2) Discussed retry/fallback, sampling, PII scrubbing, RBAC, audit logs, cost split for fallback. 3) Next steps: pricing, share logs, follow up deep-dive.

End of transcript.
